name: Wang Ren-sheng
forbes_bio: Wang Ren-sheng leads the Dennis Group, which is named after his first son and has interests in retailing, real estate and logistics.
Dennis Group's main assets are located in Henan Province in central China.
Notable properties in Zhengzhou include shopping mall David Plaza, named after his younger son.
forbes_facts: A former elementary school teacher, mainland native Wang made his early money manufacturing Christmas-tree lighting in Taiwan.

name: Fan Daidi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Fan Daidi cofounded Giant Biogene Holding with her husband, Yan Jianya, and served as its chief science officer until 2023.
The company makes collagen and other skin care products and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2022.
Fan is also vice president of Northwest University in China's Xi'an and dean of the university's Institute of Biomedical Research.
She was a senior visiting scholar at the National Center for Biological Engineering at Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1999 to 2000.
Fan also holds a stake in beauty services provider Beauty Farm Medical and Health Industry, which went public in Hong Kong in 2023.

name: Ivan Zhao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Ivan Zhao is the CEO and original founder of productivity software company Notion, which was last valued at $10 billion.
Notion's software is a minimalistic competitor to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
The software is popular among both business users and consumers. Zhao expects it to hit 100 million users in 2024.
Word-of-mouth growth has helped Zhao to keep Notion lean in employee count and profitable.
In turn, he has raised about $330 million at low dilution. He owns 30% of the company, Forbes estimates.
forbes_facts: Zhao is particular about the design and aesthetics of a space. Notion's first three offices had a no-shoes policy.
He also hand-selected every piece of furniture in Notion's San Francisco headquarters.
His favorite is the Artek Aalto Stool, designed in 1933, which retails for about $400.

name: Bobby Murphy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2019-2026); Wikidata (2017); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Bobby Murphy cofounded Snap Inc. with his Stanford University fraternity brother Evan Spiegel in 2011.
The company, known for its disappearing photo and video app Snapchat, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2017.
Murphy serves as chief technology officer while Spiegel is CEO.
Murphy and Spiegel jointly own just over 20% of Snap but have special voting shares that give them control of the company.
The son of California state employees, one of whom emigrated from the Philippines, Murphy grew up in Berkeley
forbes_facts: Before cofounding Snap, Murphy worked at Revel, a startup in San Francisco that was building management software for restaurants.

name: Guillermo Fierro
forbes_bio: Guillermo Fierro derives his fortune from a network of banks primarily in Latin America.
He is the son of Ignacio Fierro, a second-generation heir to a banking family who started its expansion in the region.
Fierro is an avid vintage car racing and competes in several races across Europe.

name: Bob Muglia
forbes_bio: Bob Muglia is an enterprise software executive and the former CEO of Snowflake, a data warehousing company. He stepped down in 2019.
Snowflake went public in a September 2020 IPO; he owns about 1.4% of Snowflake stock.
Muglia sold half of his Snowflake shares to Berkshire Hathaway as part of Snowflake's IPO.
He is currently the executive chairman of database startup Fauna and a board member at data startup Fivetran, among others.
While at Snowflake, he oversaw much of the company's growth, raising hundreds of millions in funding.

name: Sze Man Bok
forbes_bio: Sze Man Bok cofounded and chairs Hengan International, China's largest home-grown supplier of sanitary napkins.
Hengan International leads in industry sales in China over global giants such as Proctor & Gamble, Johnson & Johnson and Kimberly-Clark.
Sze's son Sze Wong Kim is a member of Hengan's board.
He cofounded the company with fellow billionaire Hui Lin Chit.

name: Ayman Hariri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Ayman Hariri is a son of the late Rafik Hariri, Lebanon's prime minister, who was assassinated while in office in 2005.
He inherited a stake in his father's Saudi-based construction company Saudi Oger, and sold it to his brother Saad in 2014.
In 2017, he sold his 42% stake in family holding company GroupeMed, which has interests in banking and real estate, for $535 million.
He invests in startups through New York-based firm Red Sea Ventures; among its investments was smart thermostat Nest, now part of Google.
He's a cofounder and CEO of Vero, an ad-free social media platform that lets users share music, videos and photos.
forbes_facts: His brother Saad Hariri also served as the prime minister of Lebanon.

name: Liu Tianwen
appears_on: Hurun Global (2024-2026); Hurun China (2024-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2021)

name: Jack Zhang
sec_insider_companies: Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (AMPH) - CEO & CHIEF SCIENTIFIC OFFICER
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Jack Zhang founded fintech company Airwallex in 2015 alongside Lucy Liu, Max Li, Jacob Dai and Ki Lok Wong.
Offering a range of online banking functions, Airwallex facilitates cross-border payments across 130 currencies and over 180 countries, serving more than 300,000 customers worldwide.
Airwallex was last valued at $11 billion in June 2026 following its $320 million Series H funding round, led by New York City-based VC firm Addition.
From its origins in a coffee shop in Melbourne, Australia, the company has expanded to 27 offices globally and is now headquartered in Singapore and San Francisco.
Born in Qingdao, China, Jack moved to Australia with his family when he was 16.
forbes_facts: Zhang says he self-funded his education through side hustles, including working in a lemon factory and bartending.

name: Nicole Grogg-Hotzer
forbes_bio: Nicole Grogg-Hotzer is the daughter of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG.
Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.
Grogg, along with her billionaire sister and mother, all serve on the board of the family's asset management firm Ingro Finanz AG.
Bachem AG develops and manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients, including peptides, amino acid derivatives and other organic molecules.
The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.
forbes_facts: In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs.

name: Kim Nam-goo
forbes_bio: Kim Nam-goo is the chief executive and largest shareholder of Korea Investment Holdings, the country's only non-bank financial holding company.
The eldest son of Dongwon founder Kim Jae-chul, Kim started at Dongwon Securities (precursor to Korea Investment Holdings) in 1991.
His brother, Kim Nam-jung, is chairman of packaged seafood producer Dongwon.
forbes_facts: When Kim was young, his father had him spend four months at sea on a deep-sea fishing vessel (Dongwon started as a tuna-processing and distribution company).

name: Song Wenguang
